question: Which invariant of how betweenness knots meet predicts the distribution of the number of orders grown by KF3 from presentations of the same line; does the second step follow Theorem 1 for every presentation with at most 11 distinctions; through which step does the bare bracketing decide the number of orders, and from which does the order of the bracketing enter?

definitions.presentation: a fewest-knot set of betweenness knots allowing exactly the line's states (a bracketing)
definitions.bare bracketing: which knot lies directly within which, from the ends' knot, forgetting which half (unlabelled rooted binary tree)
definitions.number of orders: lambda from Eppstein's formula as in STATE-RULES; two orders = lambda 2 and a bipartite crossing graph
definitions.odd set: the line distinctions whose parity a new distinction takes while no step has added a state

public_inputs.code: melib.py (sha256 9d1b32f3c600a8e489862bc14bff8a78eb0b7c925eb73adcff1635205d1788a4), job.py (sha256 ca5bd76a448d47b91b2bade3e433ccf9cb0d0c2f3a32379cd04b4b28f4af58e8), checks.py (sha256 3178f1ec7883c254837b548de7f9abf90087394d0eeace59246a96aefaa512de), merge.py (sha256 c9a376e5a9e524356d7c84c37321da931dabd8bbff32fcbb867acd0b85b8c265); numpy and networkx 3.6.1 in the workspace .venv
public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch job.py (634 cases), then merge.py on the runner output

forbidden_inputs: Changing cases, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: Predictions Q1-Q8 of research/MEET-ORDERS-20261118-001/preregistration.md, scored by merge.py.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Mirror images (identical by construction); the mutant formula and mutant criterion of checks.py; presentations of the same arrangement with different bare bracketings.

predictions.Q1: M1: Lemma B and Theorem 1 hold for every bracketing with n0 = 4..11 and every first knot
predictions.Q2: n0 = 7, 8, 9: the distribution of the number of orders at n0 + 3 depends only on the bare bracketing
predictions.Q3: n0 = 7, 8, 9: different bare bracketings give different distributions at n0 + 3
predictions.Q4: n0 = 7, 8: every two presentations that are not mirror images differ at n0 + 4
predictions.Q5: n0 = 5..9: the fewest-knot presentations are exactly the bracketings
predictions.Q6: n0 = 5..13: the chain is the unique least of Theorem 1's value
predictions.Q7: Lemma C's criterion = the measured two orders on every labelled fills-only base
predictions.Q8: n0 = 6 (to +4), 7 (to +3): labelled counts and mass by largest odd set depend only on the unrooted pair-sharing tree, and different trees differ

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as scored by merge.py

stop_rule: One run; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
runtime: 12 workers, 2 GB per case, heaviest case about 30 s; registered as MEET-ORDERS-B1 in docs/LONG_RUNNING.md.
